name: Drunkenness and Drugs

counsel.text: It is easier to obey the commands of God than sin. The commands of sin are burdensome -- let a man be under the power of any lust, how he tires himself! what hazards he runs, even to endangering his health and soul, that he may satisfy his lusts!
counsel.author: Thomas Watson

counsel.text: Consider what ways, what companies, what opportunities, what studies, what businesses, what conditions, have at any time given, or do usually give, advantages to thy distempers, and set thyself heedfully against them all. Men will do this with respect unto their bodily infirmities and distempers. The seasons, the diet, the air that have proved offensive shall be avoided. Are the things of the soul of less importance?
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: He died to destroy the works of the devil. Whatever came upon our natures by his first temptation, whatever receives strength in our persons by his daily suggestions, Christ died to destroy it all.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Holy and merciful Father, you made my body for yourself, and you call me to present it to you as a living sacrifice. I come only through Jesus Christ. I confess that I have given myself to drink and drugs. I have been mastered by what you never meant to rule me. I have run to the bottle, the pills, or the high for the comfort, courage, and rest that only you can give. I have lied to hide it, spent what was not mine to waste, hurt those who love me, and dulled the mind you gave me to know you. I have made a god of my own relief. This is sin, and it has become a chain I cannot break in my own strength. Have mercy on me, Lord. Christ drank the cup of your wrath to the dregs, so that I might lift up the cup of salvation. He came to proclaim liberty to the captives, and if the Son sets me free, I will be free indeed. For his sake forgive me. Holy Spirit, break this bondage and fill me with yourself. Give me humility to seek help from my pastor, my brethren, and those who can care for my body. I thank you that such were some of your people, and they were washed. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When the craving comes
prayers.text: Lord, the craving is strong, and I know exactly where I want to turn. Turn me to you instead. You are the fountain of living waters; do not let me go back to broken cisterns that hold no water. You have promised that no temptation has overtaken me that is not common to man, and that you will provide the way of escape. Show it to me now, and give me strength to take it. Let a brother answer when I call. Lord Jesus, you were tempted in the wilderness and did not give way; stand with me in this hour. Amen.

prayers.title: For freedom
prayers.text: Father, I am weak, but your power is made perfect in weakness. Free me from this bondage. Teach me to hate the sin and not only its consequences. Show me the people, places, money, and moods that lead me back, and give me courage to cut them off. Make me honest with my pastor and my brethren, and humble enough to accept help for my body as well as my soul. When I fall, keep me from despair, and raise me up again in Christ. Let me be filled with the Spirit and not with wine. Through Jesus Christ. Amen.

examinationQuestions: When you used today, or wanted to, what were you running from or reaching for: relief, sleep, courage, numbness, or company?
Has drink or a drug become a refuge you run to instead of God?
Are you hiding how much or how often you use, or where it comes from? Who should know the truth?
What people, places, hours, moods, or money make it easier to use, and what will you cut off?
Is your life now arranged around getting, using, or recovering, and what has that cost your family, your work, and your church?
Have you told your pastor and seen a doctor? If your body depends on it, stopping safely may need medical help.
fleeActions: Get rid of what you have on hand, and do not keep a supply for later. If your body depends on it, call a doctor today about stopping safely.
Leave the place or the people now. Do not stay to prove you can resist.
Call or text a brother or sister in your church right now and say it plainly: I want to use.
Delete the number or the app you use to get it, or ask someone you trust to hold your money and keys tonight.
Drink water, eat something, then step outside and walk, praying as you go. A craving rises and falls; this one will pass.
Call your pastor today. If you have tried to stop and cannot, ask him to help you find treatment as well.

afterFallReadings.text: Consider his mercifulness, tenderness, and kindness, as he is our great High Priest at the right hand of God. Assuredly he pities thee in thy distress; saith he, "As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you," Isa. 66:13. He hath the tenderness of a mother to a sucking child.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

afterFallReadings.text: The people of God have sins of daily occurrence; and, besides these, they sometimes lapse into great sins, and God is provoked, and his justice is ready to break forth upon them: but Christ's intercession is ready at hand, he daily makes up the breaches between God and them; he presents the merits of his blood to his Father, to pacify him.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: A Body of Divinity, Christ's priestly office

help.text: If someone may have overdosed, call 911 now; naloxone (Narcan) can reverse an opioid overdose. If your body depends on alcohol, pills, or other drugs, do not stop all at once without a doctor, because withdrawal can be dangerous. For free, confidential help at any hour, call the SAMHSA National Helpline.
help.label: Call 1-800-662-4357
